window.basis: official local fixture date (NHL gameWeek date, EuroLeague local date, MLB officialDate, WTA/PDC published date); LoL uses the feed UTC start date

method.prices: Our own originated fair prices: decimal = 1/p, no margin. No bookmaker or OLBG price is read.
method.confidence: High: model p>=0.70 (plus sample-size caps); Medium: 0.58<=p<0.70; Low: p<0.58.
method.focus_rule: Focus predictions are written for originated selections graded High whose fair American price sits inside -250..+10,000.
method.nhl: Poisson goals from shrinkage-adjusted GF/GA rates (k=8 games toward league mean), home x1.05 / away x0.95; moneyline includes OT (tie split by expected-goals share); puck line from the same score matrix; total line = nearest .5 to expected final total incl. the OT goal. A High grade additionally requires both teams to have >=8 games in the standings snapshot (one row is capped by this: Los Angeles, 7 GP).
method.euroleague: Expected points from shrinkage-adjusted PF/PA per game (k=6), derived from the 61 played scores in the official feed; Normal margin sigma 12.0 / total sigma 19.0; flat +2.2 home edge. High capped unless both teams have >=7 games in the derived sample.
method.mlb: Moneyline: log5 on 2026 home/away split win percentages. Run line/total: expected runs from RS/RA rates with a disclosed Normal approximation (diff sigma 4.1, total sigma 4.6). Probable pitchers not read.
method.pdc: Logistic on European Tour Order of Merit seed difference (k=0.035 per seed place), best-of-11 legs; confidence capped at Medium because seeding is not world ranking.
method.unpriced: Fixtures verified on an official source but lacking a verified strength input are published with blank prices and a stated reason. Unverified values are never inferred.

focus_picks.prediction: Two 5-3-1 teams with 11 points apiece meet at American Airlines Center on 25 October, and there is precious little between the New York Islanders and Dallas Stars: New York have actually scored more (27 goals to 23) while conceding only five more, and both arrive on winning streaks, the Islanders two straight and Dallas three. Our model makes Dallas a narrow favourite on home ice, projecting just 2.51 goals to 2.19, which leaves the Islanders needing only to avoid a two-goal defeat. That is exactly the shape of game their low-event profile tends to produce. Selection: New York Islanders +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -250.

Columbus Blue Jackets limp into American Airlines Center on 31 October with only six points from eight games, winless in two road outings and outscored 20 to 29 so far. Dallas Stars are the opposite story: three straight wins, a stingy 15 goals against in nine games, and 11 points banked. The gap in defensive numbers is stark — Columbus leak 3.6 goals a night against a Dallas side allowing barely half that — and our projection (3.20 expected goals to 2.01) reflects it. At home, against a side that has not won away all month, the call is straightforward. Prediction: Dallas Stars win the moneyline, our fair price -249.

Pittsburgh Penguins are home at PPG Paints Arena on 24 October but bring a decidedly leaky profile into this one: 38 goals conceded in ten games, three wins from ten, and four defeats on the bounce, even if 33 scored shows the firepower remains. Nashville Predators have quietly collected points everywhere, unbeaten in regulation on the road at 1-0-2 and 3-2-3 overall, the sort of side that keeps games tight. With expected goals at 3.32 versus 3.19 this projects as a one-score game deep into the third period. Getting a goal and a half with the steadier travellers is the value side. Selection: Nashville Predators +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -245.

Philadelphia Flyers have won three in a row, and that is where the good news ends: they have still scored just 20 goals in twelve games, the lowest per-game rate in our standings snapshot, while shipping 37, and their road mark is 1-4-1. Washington Capitals, 5-4-0 and 4-2-0 at Capital One Arena, own a far healthier balance with 30 goals for against 29 against in nine outings. Our model leans hard into that scoring contrast on 28 October, projecting 3.37 home goals to 2.17, because Philadelphia simply have not shown they can keep pace away from home. Prediction: Washington Capitals win the moneyline, our fair price -243.

On the bare records Utah Mammoth are arguably the better side in this 3 November visit to Scotiabank Arena: 7-3-0, 14 points, 38 goals scored and a winning 4-2-0 road ledger, against a Toronto Maple Leafs team at 5-4-2 whose 35 conceded is four more than Utah have allowed. Toronto's home edge and matching 38-goal attack nudge our moneyline their way, but only just — expected goals sit at 3.47 to 3.36, a virtual coin toss between two free-scoring sides. In a game this tight, the visitors with the superior points haul plus a goal and a half of insurance is the percentage play. Selection: Utah Mammoth +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -242.

Edmonton Oilers have set the early pace in our standings cut: 7-1-1 and 15 points from nine games is the best points-per-game rate in the snapshot, built on 41 goals scored and two straight wins heading towards this 5 November date at Rogers Place. Anaheim Ducks travel in the opposite direction, 4-5-0 after four consecutive defeats with a negative goal balance of 26 for and 29 against. Edmonton's attack is producing over four and a half goals a night, and our projection of 4.15 expected goals to Anaheim's 2.79 is among the widest on the whole slate. Even accounting for the gap to game day, the home side is hard to oppose. Prediction: Edmonton Oilers win the moneyline, our fair price -242.

focus_picks.competition: MLB World Series 2026 — World Series Game 3
focus_picks.prediction: The World Series shifts to Tropicana Field on 26 October and the regular-season numbers say Milwaukee Brewers, not Tampa Bay Rays, were the stronger all-round club: 103 wins to 98, 832 runs scored to 736, only 618 conceded to Tampa Bay's 650, and a run differential of +214 against +86. Tampa Bay's formidable 55-26 home record is why our moneyline still leans to the hosts, yet our run model actually projects Milwaukee to outscore them here, 4.60 expected runs to 3.87. A team we project to win the run battle outright, getting a run and a half of protection, is an easy side to land on. Selection: Milwaukee Brewers +1.5 on the run line in Game 3, our fair price -241.

focus_picks.competition: MLB World Series 2026 — World Series Game 4
focus_picks.prediction: Splits tell an interesting tale for Game 4 at Tropicana Field on 27 October: Tampa Bay Rays went 55-26 at home this year, but Milwaukee Brewers were no ordinary visitors, winning 48 of 81 on the road while posting the best scoring attack in this matchup — 832 runs in 162 games, better than five a night. Our log5 moneyline respects the Rays' home fortress, but the runs model keeps coming back to Milwaukee, whose pitching and defence also allowed the fewest runs of the two staffs at 618. One-run games are the norm at this stage of October, and the +1.5 cushion covers both the narrow defeat and the outright win our projection narrowly favours. Selection: Milwaukee Brewers +1.5 on the run line in Game 4, our fair price -241.

focus_picks.competition: MLB World Series 2026 — World Series Game 5
focus_picks.prediction: A necessary caveat first: Game 5 on 28 October is flagged if-necessary on the official schedule, so this only applies if the series is still alive. If it is, recent form tilts our view of the run line: Milwaukee Brewers closed their verified standings snapshot on a five-game winning streak and an 8-2 last-ten, whereas Tampa Bay Rays finished 5-5 over the same span. Add the season-long edges — five more wins, 96 more runs scored, 32 fewer surrendered — and Milwaukee again project around 4.6 runs to Tampa Bay's 3.9 despite playing under the Tropicana roof. Backing the form team with a run and a half in hand remains our strongest angle of this series. Selection: Milwaukee Brewers +1.5 on the run line in Game 5, our fair price -241.

Tampa Bay Lightning are the form road side arriving at Bridgestone Arena on 31 October — 7-2-0, three consecutive victories and a plus-eight goal difference — so it is no surprise our model edges the moneyline their way. But look closer and the margin is a whisker: 3.07 expected goals to Nashville Predators' 2.85, with Nashville having lost only twice in regulation through eight games and taken points in six of them at 3-2-3. The Predators simply do not get blown out: 24 goals conceded in eight games is a defensive rate barely worse than Tampa Bay's own 23 in nine. Needing Nashville merely to stay within one goal at home makes the handicap the attraction. Selection: Nashville Predators +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -241.

On 29 October at Bridgestone Arena this is close to the definition of a pick'em: Washington Capitals stand 5-4-0 with 30 goals scored in nine games, Nashville Predators 3-2-3 having collected points in six of eight, and our expected-goals figures separated by less than two tenths at 3.20 to 3.01 after home advantage. Washington's road record of 1-2-0 is the weakest line on either sheet, which is why we pass on their win price, but their superior scoring power — 30 goals to Nashville's 23 — makes a multi-goal defeat feel unlikely. With the goal and a half in hand, even another narrow road loss still lands the selection. Selection: Washington Capitals +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -240.

Chicago Blackhawks have been the session's most obliging visitors: 0-4-0 on the road, 3-6-0 overall, a minus-15 goal difference built on just 21 scored and 36 conceded in nine games. Florida Panthers are no juggernaut at 5-3-2, yet at Amerant Bank Arena on 4 November they bring a winning home record, 31 goals of their own, and double Chicago's points tally, 12 to six. Our model projects 3.75 Florida goals against a Chicago defence leaking four a night, the clearest single-team edge of that evening's card. Against a side still searching for its first away win of the season, siding with the hosts needs little further argument. Prediction: Florida Panthers win the moneyline, our fair price -235.

This 24 October meeting at Delta Center pits together two of the month's pace-setters, each on 14 points: Utah Mammoth at 7-3-0 with 38 goals in ten games, Tampa Bay Lightning at 7-2-0 with three straight wins. If anything Tampa Bay's defensive sheet is the tidier of the two, 23 conceded in nine games against Utah's 31 in ten, and our model could barely split them at 3.32 expected goals to 3.12 once home ice is counted. In a clash of equals, taking the side with fewer defeats and adding a goal and a half to their starting position is a strong proposition — Tampa Bay can lose narrowly and still reward it. Selection: Tampa Bay Lightning +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -234.

Identical 4-3-2 records and ten points apiece tell you how little separates Winnipeg Jets and Montréal Canadiens before their 3 November date at Centre Bell, and the underlying goal numbers point marginally Winnipeg's way: 26 conceded to Montréal's 34, a defence that has leaked more than three and a half goals a night. Home ice nudges our win probability towards the Canadiens, but expected goals of 3.26 to 3.04 keep this firmly in one-goal territory. Winnipeg have also been the more dependable travellers batch-for-batch at 2-1-1 away. Faced with a choice between a coin-flip win price and a goal-and-a-half cushion on the sounder defence, the handicap is clearly the smarter vehicle. Selection: Winnipeg Jets +1.5 on the puck line, our fair price -234.
